card.summary: A two‑storey red‑brick colonial home with a large front porch, swing, and two‑car garage, offering seven rooms and classic curb appeal.
card.description: The residence is a dignified two‑storey red‑brick colonial home measuring 1280 cm wide by 991 cm deep, with 2.44 m ceiling heights on each floor. Seven well‑proportioned rooms accommodate four bedrooms, a formal living room, dining area, kitchen and two full bathrooms, while a generous 400 cm deep front porch stretches the full width, providing a shaded transition from the street. The porch is finished in smooth concrete and topped with a modest timber overhang that supports a sturdy steel swing frame; a wooden swing seat hangs from steel chains, inviting leisurely afternoons. A gabled roof of asphalt shingles crowns the structure, and a two‑car side garage with a sliding steel door occupies the west elevation. Brickwork is laid in a traditional running bond, painted a vivid scarlet that catches the eye, while white trim accentuates windows and doors. Interior partitions are gypsum board, and double‑hung windows punctuate each façade, delivering balanced daylight. The house reads as a timeless yet lively presence on the neighborhood, its bold colour and welcoming porch echoing early‑20th‑century pattern‑book charm while offering modern comforts.
plan: Measure the lot dimensions and mark the building footprint of 1280 cm by 991 cm on the site.
Draft detailed construction drawings including foundation, wall sections, roof framing, porch layout and swing placement.
Excavate and pour a reinforced concrete slab foundation with integrated footings.
Erect the brick exterior walls to a height of 488 cm, install interior gypsum partitions, and frame the second‑floor joists.
Install the gabled roof trusses, apply asphalt shingle sheathing, and fit all doors, windows and the garage door.
Construct the 400 cm deep front porch, attach the steel swing frame, hang the swing seat with chains, and finish the porch flooring.
Perform final interior finishes, connect all services, and conduct a thorough inspection for code compliance.
assumptions: The brief did not specify the number of bedrooms, so four bedrooms are assumed to fit within the seven rooms typical of the Cronhardt plan.
Because no roof type was given, a gabled roof with asphalt shingles is assumed as the most common historic‑modern hybrid.
A two‑car garage is added based on the Cosgrove reference and the common need for vehicle storage in similar neighborhoods.
Interior finishes such as gypsum board walls and timber flooring are assumed to match the period‑appropriate quality of the reference designs.

card.summary: A two‑storey red‑sided colonial home with a large two‑car garage, front porch, and a double swing set in the yard.
card.description: The residence presents a dignified two‑storey colonial silhouette rendered in bright red wood siding that commands the streetscape. A generous 14.6 m by 12.7 m footprint rests on a reinforced concrete slab, its perimeter footings anchoring a robust timber frame. The gabled roof, sheathed in plywood and capped with dark asphalt shingles, rises to a peak of 7.5 m, punctuated by twelve operable sash windows that admit abundant daylight. The front elevation is anchored by a 90 cm wide painted‑wood entry door with classic hinges, while a spacious two‑car garage occupies the left wing, its 3 m wide steel sliding door providing effortless access. A welcoming front porch of 3 m by 2 m, supported by turned wooden columns, shelters a modest porch light. Inside, four bedrooms and two baths are arranged around a central hallway, each bedroom accessed by solid wood doors. The interior stairs of warm oak lead to the second floor, where a modest balcony railing frames the rear view. Outside, a double swing set—steel frame, two wooden seats, and flexible chains—anchors in the rear yard, offering playful motion against the backdrop of the red façade. Every element is dimensioned to fit within the overall envelope, with the foundation slab occupying a full third of the building’s footprint, ensuring structural integrity and ease of BIM replication.

Excavate, pour a reinforced concrete foundation slab and footings, then erect exterior wall studs and sheathing.
Install roof trusses, sheathing, and asphalt shingles, then fit windows, front door, garage door, and interior doors.
Apply red exterior paint, finish interior finishes, construct the front porch, and anchor the double swing set in the yard.
Perform a final inspection, verify code compliance, and issue the occupancy certificate.

Bedroom and bathroom counts were inferred from the reference designs, resulting in four bedrooms and two bathrooms.

card.summary: A red‑painted two‑storey colonial home with a large two‑car garage, double swing set, big couch, and wall‑mounted TV.
card.description: This two‑storey red‑painted wood residence measures 1,585 cm wide by 838 cm deep, echoing the classic 1920s colonial proportions of the Delwood pattern. A generous gable roof capped with asphalt shingles crowns the structure, while a spacious front porch of 300 cm × 200 cm invites guests onto the painted façade. Inside, six well‑proportioned rooms—including three bedrooms and two full baths—are framed with timber studs and finished with oak hardwood flooring. The attached two‑car garage, 360 cm wide, dominates the rear elevation and provides ample storage for a vehicle and tools. A double swing set, anchored in concrete footings at the front yard, offers a playful flexing motion for two children. The living room showcases a large, upholstered couch (250 cm × 100 cm) positioned for conversation, and a 150 cm‑wide flat‑screen TV mounted on the wall for effortless viewing. All windows and doors retain original wood frames, painted to match the red exterior, and the interior is finished with a subtle red accent paint that ties the exterior hue to the interior ambience. Modern conveniences—electrical, plumbing, and HVAC—are concealed within the walls, delivering contemporary comfort within a historic silhouette.
plan: Measure the lot, note setbacks, and record existing utilities before any drawing begins.
Draft schematic floor plans and elevations in CAD, then refine them into construction documents with dimensions in centimetres.
Submit the plans for building permits, schedule inspections, and order long‑lead items such as roof trusses and garage doors.
Excavate, pour a reinforced concrete slab foundation, and install perimeter footings to support the two‑storey frame.
Erect the wood frame, raise wall studs, install floor joists, roof trusses, and then sheathe the exterior with plywood.
Fit windows, exterior doors, and the double‑car garage door, then apply red exterior paint and install the gable roof with shingles.
Run electrical, plumbing, and HVAC services, finish interior walls, lay hardwood flooring, and place the big couch and wall‑mounted TV.
Install the double swing set in the front yard, anchor its posts, and attach swing seats with chains.
Perform the final walkthrough, correct any punch‑list items, and issue the certificate of occupancy.
assumptions: The house follows the Delwood plan: two storeys, six rooms, two full bathrooms, and a front porch.
Three bedrooms are allocated: master on the second floor and two secondary bedrooms on the first floor.
The roof is a traditional gable covered with asphalt shingles, matching typical 1920s colonial roofs.
The garage is sized for two cars (approximately 360 cm wide) and is attached to the left side of the house.
questions: Do you prefer the garage to be attached on the left side, right side, or centered behind the house?
What material and finish would you like for the double swing set—treated wood, metal, or a combination?
What screen size and mounting height do you envision for the wall‑mounted TV in the living room?
